builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MATE: Mobile Agent Trustworthy Execution for Safe and Efficient Mobile Control
summary: MATE replaces direct execution of raw LLM-proposed mobile UI actions with a structured action record passed through a runtime guardrail (allow, block, or user-approval) plus predefined verified routes for recurring tasks, without modifying the underlying model. The cost is engineering effort to define the action schema, risk policies, verified routes, and post-execution screen checks, plus an approval step that adds user friction for flagged actions. It can fail when the guardrail's policy mapping misclassifies novel actions, when predefined routes break under UI changes in target apps, or when screen-context extraction is incomplete.
rationale: The guardrail and routing layers operate at the execution boundary without model changes, so a small team using API models can adopt them, but the gains depend on the specific app workflows and risk taxonomy and require workload-specific validation.
technique: Execution-layer guardrails and verified routing for mobile agents

claims.statement: MATE replaces direct execution of raw LLM-proposed mobile UI actions with a structured action record passed through a runtime guardrail (allow, block, or user-approval) plus predefined verified routes for recurring tasks, without modifying the underlying model. The cost is engineering effort to define the action schema, risk policies, verified routes, and post-execution screen checks, plus an approval step that adds user friction for flagged actions. It can fail when the guardrail's policy mapping misclassifies novel actions, when predefined routes break under UI changes in target apps, or when screen-context extraction is incomplete.
On AndroidWorld, Predefined Task Routing reduces LLM calls by up to 6x and raises recurring-use task success to 95.7%; on MobileSafetyBench, high-risk blocking rises from 29.7% to 97.0% under GPT-4o.
